newsitem.title: UK: Exxon Corp signs China power deal memorandum.
newsitem.headline: Exxon Corp signs China power deal memorandum.

text.p: U.S. oil giant Exxon Corp said on Thursday its Exxon Energy Ltd unit and Duke Energy had signed a memorandum of understanding with China's Huaneng Group to jointly develop, own and operate power projects in China.
Both Duke Energy, part of Duke Power Co, and Exxon Energy, are based in Hong Kong and have been pursuing Chinese power development ventures under a joint venture deal signed in March.

The memorandum focuses on greenfield, or to-be-constructed projects, and expansion of existing power facilities, Exxon said in a statement released in London. The companies will explore both coal and natural gas-fired opportunities.
China Huaneng Group is a state-owned firm that develops, builds and operates power plants and sells electricity to China's local provincial power bureaus.
It has 17,325 megawatts of capacity, representing eight percent of China's installed capacity.
